- It comes from PR #23674's merge-queue build `38746430608` (comment `6194362903` on that PR).
- The same package went red on that PR's `pull_request` run and on this card's schedule run.
- **#23685's reading (not measured):** the pin's `beforeAll` seeds 2,700 + 2,700 rows one `create` at a time, and the `it` runs three full scans against a composed `$in` over 2,400 parents with vitest's 5,000 ms default.

#23685 is `pm:blocked` on this card. It is not folded in, because this card is in flight. Measuring that evaluation in this round decides whether #23685 closes with this card or carries a product fix.

Step 2 reading · `domain:engine` seat 1, dispatched dev, branch `claude/issue-23679-driver-memory-full-run-red` · `session_01GP3comALHRcRBixS2TEnLF` · 2026-10-15T15:05Z · ⛔ not a claim · no code changed yet

## The failing tests and their error

Both are in `packages/drivers/driver-memory/src/memory-readable-ids-conformance.test.ts` (added by #23656), under `[ADR-0139 D3] InMemoryDriver — ReadableIds conformance` › `E3 pins`:

- `a deleted parent is excluded, on find, count and aggregate alike`
- `a reader with 2400 readable candidates gets every visible row, and count equals the rows served`

The error is the same for both: `Error: Test timed out in 5000ms.` This is vitest's default per-test timeout. No assertion failed.

**How they were named.** The CI log line itself is still unread. It is past the MCP reader's 5,000-line window, and the log's blob host refused this container again (`CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403`). So the two tests are named by the reproduction below. The package's per-test durations show why no other test can be the one: the next slowest test takes 248–280 ms.

## Reproduction rate

All runs were on `8d1fb1fb2d`, in a detached worktree, in a 4-vCPU container shared with two sibling devs.

| Shape | Runs | Red | Reading |
|:--|--:|--:|:--|
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/driver-memory test` | 3 | 0 | 1732/1732 each time. The two pins took 2.7–3.2 s and 1.7–2.1 s, which is 54–64% of the 5,000 ms budget. |
| `turbo run test test:repo --filter=@objectstack/driver-memory --concurrency=4 --continue=dependencies-successful` | 3 | 0 | Run with `--cache=local:r`, so the test task really ran each time. Every log reads `cache miss, executing`. |
| The shard's CPU share: the package's own suite with 3 workers, pinned to one core (`taskset -c 0 … vitest run --maxWorkers=3`) | 2 | 2 | Each run failed exactly these two tests (6.5–8.9 s and 10.4–10.7 s). Every other test was green. |

**Why the third shape is the shard's.** The whole-packages leg of `Test Core (4/6)` runs 4 packages at once (`--concurrency=4`), each with vitest's default 3 workers, on the runner's 4 vCPUs. That is up to 3 busy workers per core. On this commit, `partition-test-shards.mjs --shard 4/6` places `driver-memory` in a 21-item set beside `driver-sql`, `plugin-auth`, `example-showcase` and `driver-mongodb`.

## Mechanism (measured)

- **One read is about 1 second.** A probe timed a single composed-leaf read over the E3 fixture (2,700 child rows, 2,400 readable parents) at about 1,070 ms. About 945 ms of that is mingo evaluating the rewritten `$in` list of 2,400 ids.
- **mingo re-hashes the whole list for every row.** mingo's `$in` calls `intersection([value, list])` once per document, and `intersection` builds a hash map of the entire list each time. So one read costs rows × ids hash inserts.
- **A prebuilt set takes 0.8 ms.** The same member test over the same rows, against one set built once, takes 0.8 ms.
- **Each pin makes several such reads.** The two pins make 3 and 2 reads in one test, so they sit at 1.7–3.2 s on an idle-ish box, against a 5 s budget.

**So the red can recur.** It is a load race against vitest's 5,000 ms default. The driver's per-row re-hashing of the `$in` list carries it, and it needs no other merge in the range. H2 is not supported: every red is a timeout, and the uncontended runs pass every assertion.

## Next

The fix goes at the producer, in `driver-memory`. The driver's mingo `$in` will hash its list once per compiled query, with the semantics otherwise unchanged. A deterministic pin will count hash inserts, and an ablation will show the pin goes red without the fix. ⛔ No timeout raise, skip, retry, quarantine or battery change.
